correctness.rationale: The three perfect matchings give the exact \((2,2)\) Laplacian eigenvalues \(W\pm\sqrt\Delta\). Sign twisting gives \(\lambda_{(2,1,1)}=2W-\Lambda\), where \(\Lambda\) is the top eigenvalue of the three-dimensional restriction of the ordinary Laplacian. Its diagonal entries are \(W-a,W-b,W-c\), and the off-diagonal entries are bundle differences, giving trace \(2W\) and squared Frobenius trace at most \(W^2+3T\). The three-eigenvalue deviation inequality yields \(\Lambda\le 2W/3+2\sqrt{W^2+3\Delta}/3\le(4W+2\sqrt\Delta)/3\) for \(0\le\Delta\le W^2\). Thus \(\lambda_{(2,1,1)}\ge 2\lambda_{(2,2)}/3\) for all nonnegative rates, including disconnected cases. All other dominance pairs follow from Aldous or the sign-representation upper bound \(2W\). The unit star attains ratio \(2/3\). Eight symbolic identities and 2053 seeded numerical rate-vector tests replay successfully; finite checks do not replace the universal algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 source explicitly formulates the \(2/3\) inequality as conjectural for arbitrary graphs. Its all-weight theorem gives only \(n^{-3}\) and its \(2/3\) theorem is restricted to quasi-complete rates. Its star equality is known and not claimed new. The 2013 exact Aldous-order paper treats the distinct constant-one order, including its four-vertex failure. Targeted semantic research results and accessible prior claim IDs revealed no dominating exact six-rate \(n=4\) bound. value.rationale: The unrestricted weighted \(n=4\) case is a natural first nontrivial complete case of an explicitly open uniform spectral-comparison conjecture: it treats six continuous parameters and precisely the pair where the older constant-one order fails. The exact sharp inequality and its three-dimensional Frobenius mechanism are mathematically stronger than finite unweighted tests and may guide higher-order problems. The fact is valuable as a sharp complete case without asserting a general-order theorem.
